prerequisites: The specialized seminars generally refer to content from specific compulsory or advanced modules that should have been completed beforehand.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have in-depth scientific knowledge in the selected seminar topic.
Students have practically practiced giving a scientific presentation and can independently convey research results in a didactically well-prepared presentation.
Participants can formulate and receive constructive feedback.
Students can write a written elaboration on their seminar presentation.

syllabus_topics: Bachelor seminars on several relevant topics in IT security, such as network and data security, implementation security, human-centered security and privacy, or cryptography. Students choose a topic based on their interests and individual specialization wishes. This topic should be worked on independently. This includes literature research, familiarization with the topic, and finally the presentation. Further information can be found in the course catalog for the respective seminars.
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded for a successful seminar presentation and, if applicable, a written elaboration. Continuous active participation in the dialogical exchange between teachers and students is essential. Attendance at presentation dates is obligatory for all participants. Lecturers can define additional mandatory dates before the start of the event. Absenteeism should not exceed 25% of the mandatory appointments, except for specific dates (e.g., Kick-Off Meeting, own presentation date) where absence requires justification (e.g., medical certificate). Exceeding allowed absences results in failing the seminar, though withdrawal is possible with a medical certificate for illness-related absences.
